title: HybridRAG: A Fusion of Graph and Vector Retrieval  - Mitesh Patel, NVIDIA
talk_summary: NVIDIA talk presents HybridRAG: build a vector index plus an LLM-extracted knowledge graph, retrieve with multi-hop graph and vector search, evaluate with Ragas, and tune extraction and latency. It is a document-RAG architecture, not agent orchestration; transferable pieces are eval discipline, schema/cleaning for extraction, and retrieval-depth/latency tradeoffs.

takeaways.what_they_do: Use Ragas to score query interpretation, retrieval, and final response separately so retrieval failures are visible.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it evaluates the response. It evaluates the retrieval and it evaluates what the query is.

takeaways.what_they_do: Combine semantic vector chunks with an LLM-extracted entity/relationship graph so retrieval can follow multi-hop links.
Define an ontology in the extraction prompt, clean punctuation/noise, shorten outputs, and fine-tune the extractor.
takeaways.numbers: 71% to 87% accuracy on 100 documents after LoRA and tweaks

takeaways.technique: Cap graph hop depth against latency
takeaways.what_they_do: Tune single-hop vs multi-hop retrieval to a latency sweet spot and use accelerated graph search.

takeaways.technique: Fine-tune small extractor for structured outputs
takeaways.what_they_do: Fine-tune a Llama model with LoRA to generate cleaner triplets instead of relying only on prompt engineering with a larger model.
